market_summary: Nasdaq -5.2% (now in correction) and S&P 500 -3.9% on Nov 5, the S&P's worst day since April 2025. Chips had their worst day since March 2020 (SOXX about -11%) on fears that the Democratic midterm sweep and a proposed data-centre moratorium will slow AI capex. Investors moved into Treasuries: the 10-year fell to 4.83% and the 2-year dropped 10bp. Odds of a December Fed hike fell to about 70% from 83%, although Barkin still expects gradual hikes. Oil fell more than 8% overnight on hopes that the Qatar-brokered Iran talks end the war, and Alibaba rose while US tech fell.

AMZN.reason: Down 2.6% in the tech selloff. Much smaller move than chips. Forward P/E about 26.

AXOS.reason: Down 1.9% with the broader market. No company news. Forward P/E about 9.

BABA.reason: Up 1.4% while US tech fell. Not exposed to the US data-centre politics. Forward P/E about 13.

ENPH.reason: Down 10% in a risk-off session. No company-specific news found. Forward P/E about 28.

FIGR.reason: Down 10% as small caps (Russell 2000 -4.6%) fell into correction. Q3 results expected mid-November.

GOOGL.reason: Down 2% while chips fell 9-15%. Forward P/E about 21.

LDI.reason: Down 7%. Lower Treasury yields help mortgage lenders, but the stock trades on sentiment. No forward P/E shown.

META.reason: Down 4% on concerns about AI capex and debt. Forward P/E about 18.

MRVL.reason: Down 14%, one of the worst holdings, as AI infrastructure names sold off. Forward P/E about 24.

MU.reason: Down 15%. Memory names were hit hardest (SanDisk -20%). Forward P/E under 4 points to peak-earnings pricing.

NFLX.reason: Down 1.6%. Not tied to AI capex. Forward P/E about 18.

NVDA.reason: Down about 9% as semis had their worst day since March 2020. Forward P/E about 15.

RKT.reason: Down 1.7%. A 6bp fall in the 10-year yield helps mortgage demand. Forward P/E about 25.

TSM.reason: Down about 10% with the chip sector. No company news. Forward P/E about 17.

STRIPE.reason: Private. No new valuation reported this run.

OPENAI.reason: Private. The selloff in public AI infrastructure names and Sanders' call for a data-centre moratorium are risks to AI funding. No new valuation reported.

headlines: Chips have their worst day since March 2020: MU -15%, MRVL -14%, NVDA and TSM about -10% intraday.
Nasdaq down about 5% into correction on fear of data-centre pauses after the Democratic sweep; no law exists yet.
GPU rents still at highs: H100 $2.97/hr, B200 $6.70, up 6-14% on the week while the stocks fall.
10-yr falls to 4.83% and December hike odds slip to about 70%; rate-sensitive names still fell.
